scan.summary: This is a blank inspection checklist, not a permit, record or program. Every field is empty: facility, permit number, inspection date, inspector, all Yes/No/N.A. answers, evidence, notes and signatures. It proves nothing about Cascade yet. Its real use is as a list of what an inspector would ask to see. Lines A1–C5 cover the permit, renewal timing, annual and semi-annual reports, deviation reporting, scrubber and carbon-unit records, opacity monitoring, keeping records for 5 years, and conditions on the day of inspection.
scan.freshness_note: The form has no date, no form number and no revision marking, and no inspection has been recorded on it. If an inspection has actually happened, ask DEQ or the inspector for the completed, signed copy. As a prep tool, check each line against the permit itself (Standard ACDP 26-2841-ST-01), not against this form.

deadlines.title: Annual report for calendar year 2026 (the form says it is due by February 15; confirm the date in the permit)
deadlines.source_line: A3 — Annual report for the previous calendar year submitted by February 15

deadlines.title: Semi-annual monitoring report for January–June 2026 (the form says it was due July 31, which has passed; check that it was filed, and confirm in the permit that such a report is required)
deadlines.source_line: A4 — Semi-annual monitoring report for January to June submitted by July 31

deadlines.title: Deviation reporting: notify within 24 hours and report in writing within 15 days of any deviation (according to the form; confirm in the permit)
deadlines.source_line: A5 — Deviation reports: any deviation in the last 12 months notified within 24 hours and reported in writing within 15 days

deadlines.title: Permit renewal application: the form says at least 120 days before expiry. Confirm the lead time in the permit and in OAR 340-216; I am not sure 120 days is right for a Standard ACDP.
deadlines.source_line: A2 — Renewal application submitted at least 120 days before the permit expiration date, where expiration is within 12 months

scan.confidence_notes: I am sure the form is entirely blank and records no findings, so I did not judge it and took no company facts from it. I am less sure where it came from. The file name suggests an auditor's or consultant's version rather than a published DEQ form. It has no DEQ form number. Line C4 asks for employee count for 'fee tier verification', but I do not believe Oregon ACDP fees are based on employee count, so treat that line with caution. The 120-day renewal lead time, the February 15 and July 31 due dates and the 24-hour/15-day deviation timing all come from this form, not from the permit or the rules. Confirm each one against Standard ACDP 26-2841-ST-01 before relying on it. The equipment named on the form (tanks T-3 to T-6, carbon unit, scrubbers) matches this company, so I assigned it to the Portland site, but that is my inference; the facility field is blank.

OREGON DEQ — AIR QUALITY PROGRAM

AIR CONTAMINANT DISCHARGE PERMIT — COMPLIANCE INSPECTION CHECKLIST (INSPECTOR'S FIELD FORM)

Facility: ____________________________ Permit number: ______________ Inspection date: __________

Inspector: ____________________________ Facility contact: ____________________________

Instructions: complete each line from documents presented by the facility and from observation on the day. "Evidence seen" names the document, record or observation. A line answered from a verbal statement alone is marked Not Verified.

SECTION A — PERMIT AND SUBMISSIONS

Line

Item

Yes / No / N.A.

Evidence seen

Notes

A1

Current ACDP permit available at the facility and not expired

A2

Renewal application submitted at least 120 days before the permit expiration date, where expiration is within 12 months

A3

Annual report for the previous calendar year submitted by February 15

A4

Semi-annual monitoring report for January to June submitted by July 31

A5

Deviation reports: any deviation in the last 12 months notified within 24 hours and reported in writing within 15 days

SECTION B — RECORDS

Line

Item

Yes / No / N.A.

Evidence seen

Notes

B1

Scrubber pressure-drop log covering the last 12 months, one reading per operating day, readings within the permitted range

B2

Quarterly scrubber inspection records for the last four quarters

B3

Carbon replacement record within the last 12 months, or breakthrough records showing replacement was not required

B4

Weekly detector-tube check records at the carbon unit outlet

B5

Opacity observation records, or a statement of the method used to monitor visible emissions

B6

Records retained for five years and available on request

SECTION C — ON THE DAY

Line

Item

Yes / No / N.A.

Evidence seen

Notes

C1

Each scrubber operating with the associated line, pressure drop within range at the time of inspection

C2

Solvent storage tanks T-3 to T-6 vented to the carbon unit, no open vents or leaks observed

C3

Tank and line labels legible; permitted sources match the permit's equipment list

C4

Facility employee count on the day, for fee tier verification

C5

Emergency contact and emergency plan available at the facility

Inspector's summary: ______________________________________________________________________________

Inspector signature: ____________________ Facility signature: ____________________ Date: __________
